lead.headline: WAYMO WINS BIG WITH MASSIVE DRIVERLESS EXPANSION ACROSS AMERICA
lead.summary: In a stunning acceleration of driverless technology, Waymo has announced the expansion of its fully autonomous taxi service to four more American cities. The fleet currently handles an astonishing half a million paid rides weekly, representing a tenfold increase over just two years. With eyes on the prize, the company aims to hit a milestone of one million rides per week before the year closes out.

stories.headline: Tesla Cybercab Begins Employee Rides in Texas
stories.summary: Tesla has announced that employee test rides for its wheel-less, pedal-less Cybercab are starting soon at Giga Texas. However, the initial phase of this highly anticipated robotaxi rollout is strictly confined to a local parking lot.

stories.headline: NHTSA Demands Waymo and Tesla Fix Robotaxi Safety Kinks
stories.summary: Federal regulators are turning up the heat on self-driving pioneers. The NHTSA warned that both Waymo and Tesla must address dangerous issues with their autonomous vehicles before the national fleet expands further.

stories.headline: Tesla Faces New Jersey Robotaxi Ban Threat
stories.summary: A new legislative bill in New Jersey threatens to ban self-driving vehicles that do not utilize radar and lidar sensors, targeting Tesla's vision-only approach. Despite the domestic hurdle, Tesla continues to gain critical market share in China.

stories.headline: Police Search Waymo Cab Over Underage Riders
stories.summary: San Mateo police officers recently searched a Waymo robotaxi after the company flagged two underage passengers inside the vehicle. The incident highlights the active role of Waymo's in-cabin cameras and remote monitoring agents.

stories.headline: Robotic Pods Proposed for Automated Robotaxi Pit Stops
stories.summary: Aseon Labs is designing robotic pods to clean, charge, and inspect autonomous taxis closer to active passenger zones. The concept promises faster turnaround times but presents cities with complex zoning and placement questions.

lead.headline: META RETREATS ON INSTAGRAM AI PHOTO GRAB AFTER FIERCE BACKLASH
lead.summary: In a sudden about-face, social media giant Meta has pulled a controversial feature from its new Muse Image tool that allowed public Instagram photos to be scraped for AI generation. The retreat comes a mere three days after the tool was switched on, with executives admitting they 'missed the mark.' Critics and creators alike are celebrating the swift reversal as a win for digital privacy.

stories.headline: Beijing Warns of IP Theft in Claude Code
stories.summary: Chinese authorities have issued a stark risk advisory warning that Anthropic's Claude Code tool contains hidden monitoring mechanisms. Officials claim the tool automatically transmits sensitive user data, including geographical locations and identities.

stories.headline: Tech Giants Target Tribal Lands for Data Centers
stories.summary: Advocacy group Honor the Earth reports that big tech companies are increasingly eyeing Native American tribal lands for massive data center expansions. At least 37 projects have been mapped, sparking growing resistance from tribal communities.

stories.headline: Electricians and Grid Crews Rule the AI Boom
stories.summary: Nvidia chief Jensen Huang warns that the real bottleneck in the AI race is physical infrastructure, not just silicon chips. The prediction has propelled industrial contractor Quanta Services to a record-breaking $48 billion backlog.

stories.headline: Bank of America Warns AI Spending Fuels Inflation
stories.summary: A new financial analysis reveals that the massive investment boom in artificial intelligence is adding 0.4 percentage points to U.S. inflation. Analysts name South Korea and the UAE as top contenders rising alongside the domestic surge.

stories.headline: Experts Flee Online Communities as AI Degrades Quality
stories.summary: New research shows that the arrival of AI tools is causing a 'knowledge reset' on platforms like Stack Overflow. Expert contributors are abandoning these online hubs as automated content causes quality to decay exponentially.

stories.headline: Researchers Warn AI Is Eroding Student Math Skills
stories.summary: A newly detected phenomenon termed 'cognitive surrender' is raising alarms among educators. Studies show that students relying on AI to solve word problems are suffering from a steep decline in overall mathematical capabilities.
